newsitem.title: USA: Amgen falls on Epogen, Leptin news.
newsitem.headline: Amgen falls on Epogen, Leptin news.

text.p: Shares of Amgen Inc fell sharply Tuesday after the company forecast slowing sales growth of its Epogen drug and released data on its obesity drug candidate that analysts called "disappointing."
Amgen said Phase I trials of the leptin protein found that it had "an acceptable safety profile" and induced weight loss at certain dose levels.
The company also said the 1997 sales growth rate of Epogen would slow modestly from the 1996 growth rate of 21 percent, due to changes in the Medicare reimbursement policy.

Brown Brothers Harriman analyst Robert LeBoyer said Amgen's data on leptin was "clearly not very encouraging." Although the trial was designed to test only the safety of the compound, he said the amounts of weight lost by trial subjects -- about four to nine pounds over a 90-day period -- was not that much.
LeBoyer said the forecast for an Epogen sales slowdown "was not helping" Amgen's stock, although many analysts had already been forecasting such a trend.
Epogen, which boosts red blood cell count and is used by kidney dialysis patients, had 1996 sales of $1.072 billion.
